items.title: Gene Bertoncini interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: And the rhythm section for Peter Matz and the ‘Kraft Music Hall” was Derek Smith, Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and myself.

ctx.x: You guys kind of worked out who was going to do what nights is that right?

Yeah. And during my tenure there for a whole year I did a show called “That Was the Week That Was,” for NBC and then occasionally the “Kraft Music Hall.” And the rhythm section for Peter Matz and the ‘Kraft Music Hall” was Derek Smith, Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and myself. And all the dates with Don Elliott in recording dates on Madison Avenue, it was always Mel Lewis and Richard Davis and myself. And boy I’ve been through a lot of — you know when you think about just falling into things. And I was a pretty…

time the Bossa Nova came in. And I was very friendly with Joao Gilberto. He used to borrow my guitar to do concerts. And I learned how to do bossa nova from his records. And I just had barely started to play that way and I got a call from Ahmad Jamal to do a big date on Samba rhythms and I said, “Sure, I’ll do it.” And when I listen to Joao’s record of “Quiet Nights” and then I just took that little bit of information, the basic bossa nova beat, to Rudy VanGelder’s studio in New Jersey and it was Richard Evans’…
